newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Turk Cypriot leader says may not go to U.N. talks.
newsitem.headline: Turk Cypriot leader says may not go to U.N. talks.

text.p: Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Dentash said on Tuesday he may pull out of face-to-face talks with Cyprus President Glafcos Clerides if any document is put on the table before he has been informed of its contents.

"I am thinking of not going to New York if a document whose contents are unknown is put on the table," Denktash told reporters as he entered a special closed session of parliament in the self-proclaimed Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus.

Denktash and Clerides are due to meet next week for the first time in three years for U.N.-sponsored talks in New York, which the United Nations hopes will aid progress towards ending the island's division.

Denktash said he had asked the U.N. special representative in Cyprus, Gustave Feissel, to give him information on a document which was expected to be produced ahead of the talks, but had not received a reply.
"In view of this, personally I intend not to go to New York, but I'll discuss the issue with parliament," Denktash said.

Denktash said such a document would lend support to Clerides and said it was significant that news of the document emerged after a meeting of the Greek Cypriot foreign minister and a U.N. representative.

Feissel told the Turkish Cypriot Bayrak radio on Tuesday that the document was aimed at helping the two leaders in their negotiations and that it would probably not be completed until shortly before the meeting in New York starting on July 9.
Cyprus has been divided since 1974 when troops from Turkey invaded the island's north in reaction to a Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military junta ruling Athens at the time.
The two communities have been estranged since 1963, when a government comprising Greek and Turkish Cypriots fell apart little more then three years after independence from Britain.
The breakaway Turkish Cypriot state in the north is recognised only by Turkey.
